name: TN-04
label: Likely R

key_factors: District leans about eleven points Republican and incumbent Scott DesJarlais is running again
DesJarlais holds a large money advantage: roughly $495,000 on hand versus under $9,000 for Democrat Victoria Broderick
No public polls or expert ratings; prediction markets price Democratic chances at only a few percent
Two independents on the ballot show minimal fundraising and are unlikely to alter the two-party margin
model.rationale: Every available signal points the same way: the seat sits in an R+11 district, the incumbent is well funded while the Democratic nominee has almost no cash, and prediction markets give Democrats only a small chance of an upset. With no polling to contradict the fundamentals, a double-digit Republican margin is the reasonable read.
model.watch: Any late poll showing a single-digit race, or significant outside spending against DesJarlais, would be the first sign this is closer than the fundamentals suggest.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Tennessee's 4th District is a strongly Republican seat in southern Middle Tennessee, with a partisan lean of roughly eleven points toward the GOP. Scott DesJarlais, the incumbent since 2011, is seeking another term and holds a decisive financial edge: he has raised about $537,000 and still reports roughly $495,000 on hand, while Democratic nominee Victoria Broderick has raised about $84,000 with under $9,000 remaining. Two independents appear on the ballot but show little campaign activity.

No public polls or expert ratings cover this race, and prediction markets give Democrats only a two to four percent chance of an upset. The district lean, incumbency, and the fundraising gap all point the same direction, so the evidence supports a Republican win by a comfortable double-digit margin, with uncertainty somewhat elevated because direct polling is absent.
